title: Archival Strategy for Media Production Houses
business: A boutique media production house managing high-resolution raw footage for completed client projects.
problem: The studio faces escalating storage costs by keeping all raw project files in standard S3 buckets, despite the fact that 95% of these files are never accessed after the final delivery to the client.
solution: By implementing S3 Lifecycle policies, the studio can automatically transition older, inactive objects from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval or S3 Glacier Deep Archive, significantly reducing storage overhead while maintaining data durability.
steps: Identify project folders that have not been modified for over 90 days.
Configure an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition objects from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
Verify that the transition occurs automatically based on the object age filter.
Implement an S3 Inventory report to track which objects have successfully moved to the archival tier.
outcome: The studio achieves a sustainable cost structure for long-term data retention without needing to manually manage file migrations or delete historical assets.
limitation: A primary limitation is the retrieval time and potential cost associated with accessing archived data; users must verify if the chosen class meets their specific recovery time objectives by checking the S3 storage class documentation for retrieval latency.
